standfirst: The crustacean nodaviruses — Macrobrachium rosenbergii nodavirus, Penaeus vannamei nodavirus and covert mortality nodavirus. ICTV ratifies no genus for them, so the module is named for its most-sampled species. What separates it from Betanodavirus is a single missing gene: there is no B1, in the literature or in any of the three RefSeqs.

modules.Macrobrachium_rosenbergii_nodavirus: Three features. RNA1 carries protein A and B2 in a shifted overlapping frame; RNA2 carries one uncleaved capsid. The capsid window is genuinely bimodal by species — MrNV 371 aa, PvNV 368, CMNV 437 — so it spans both classes and is not a median.

gaps: B1 is probed for and returns ABSENT, which is the expected and required result: its absence is the organisational difference that gives this group its own module. The one reported capsid cleavage, at Arg26, is an E. coli cysteine protease artefact of recombinant expression blocked by E-64 (PMID 34445426), and is not modelled.
derived: No mature peptides. The virion capsid is a single 43 kDa polypeptide (PMID 15660790) and these viruses “do not encode a gamma-peptide” (PMID 30346944).

why.B2: Annotated Non-structural protein B2, not RNA silencing suppressor protein. Suppressor activity is demonstrated for alphanodavirus B2 (PMID 12016316) and betanodavirus B2 (PMID 16352533) and has not been shown for MrNV, PvNV or CMNV. Nor is a subgenomic RNA claimed, because none has been demonstrated for any of the three.
